description: MCP Gateway: tool calls, access, backends, resource state and reconcilers

panels.title: Gateway replicas up
panels.description: Gateway targets Prometheus currently scrapes successfully. Every replica serves traffic.

panels.title: Failed tool calls
panels.description: Share of forwarded calls that returned a tool error or never completed. Empty while there is no traffic.

panels.title: Backends unavailable
panels.description: Backends whose most recent discovery failed on every gateway replica. The Backends row shows each one, taking the worst replica instead.

panels.title: Grants not ready
panels.description: MCPGrants whose Ready condition is False or Unknown: some subject does not get everything its grant names.

panels.title: Denied calls
panels.description: tools/call requests for a tool the subject holds no grant on. A steady rate is usually an agent configured with tools it was never granted.

panels.title: Tool Call Outcomes
panels.description: ok: the tool ran and succeeded. tool_error: the tool ran and reported an error — the backend's business. backend_error: the call never completed, or the backend refused it as a protocol error. unauthorized: the backend refused the credentials of the call, or the gateway could not obtain them.

panels.title: Tool Call Latency by Server
panels.description: End to end, from the gateway receiving the call to the backend's answer.

panels.title: Failing Tools
panels.description: Only tools that failed in the window. An empty graph means nothing failed, not missing data.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (server, tool, le) (rate(mcp_gateway_tool_call_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$gateway", namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Denied Calls by Subject
panels.description: Calls refused for want of a grant, by the authenticated subject that made them. The tool name is in the gateway's audit log, not here: it is caller input, and a label made of it would be unbounded.

panels.title: Refused Tokens by Reason
panels.description: missing_token is normal in small amounts: MCP clients probe without a token to discover where to get one. unavailable means the JWKS or introspection endpoint could not be reached — the OAuth provider, not the callers.
Per backend, whether discovery works — as the gateway sees it, taking the worst replica. A backend that stays red longer than --catalog-max-age drops out of agents' tool lists.
panels.title: Backend Availability
Discovery Failures by Server
panels.description: Failed catalog reads, by the controller and every gateway replica together.

panels.title: Discovered Tools by Server
panels.description: Catalog size as last discovered. A step is a backend that published a changed catalog.

panels.title: Resources Not Ready
panels.description: Kinds with at least one resource whose Ready condition is False or Unknown. False and Unknown report zero rather than disappearing, so an empty graph means healthy, not missing data. kubectl get mcp-gateway says which ones, and why.

panels.title: Reconcile Rate by Controller
panels.description: The controller's four reconcilers, and the gateway's two read-only ones: catalog and policy.

panels.title: Reconcile Latency p95 by Controller
panels.description: Discovery happens inside the mcpserver and catalog reconcilers, so their latency is the backends' tools/list latency.

panels.title: K8s API Request Rate by Code
panels.description: The gateway only reads, through its informers. The controller writes status — one patch per server per discovery interval, and one per changed condition otherwise.

panels.title: Inspect Requests by Operation
panels.description: missing_token is normal in small amounts: MCP clients probe without a token to discover where to get one. unavailable means the JWKS or introspection endpoint could not be reached — the OAuth provider, not the callers.

panels.title: Inspect Latency p95 by Operation
panels.description: End to end, from the gateway receiving the call to the backend's answer.

panels.title: Refused Inspect Tokens by Reason
panels.description: missing_token is normal in small amounts: MCP clients probe without a token to discover where to get one. unavailable means the JWKS or introspection endpoint could not be reached — the OAuth provider, not the callers.

panels.title: Goroutines by Pod
panels.description: Every open agent session holds a few goroutines in the gateway, and so does every backend session. A gateway whose count only grows is keeping sessions nobody closes; see --session-timeout.

targets.expr: max by (component, pod, version, commit, built_at, go_version) (mcp_gateway_build_info{job=~"$controller|$gateway", namespace=~"$namespace"})

title: MCP Gateway
